fundamentals.name: Arm Holdings plc
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Arm Holdings plc researches, develops, licenses, and markets central processing unit (CPU) intellectual property (IP), graphics processing unit IP, systems IP, compute subsystems (CSS), and associated software, tools and related services. The company provides a product portfolio, including CPU IP, GPU and neural processing unit (NPU) accelerators, system IP such as interconnects, compute platform products including pre-integrated CSSs, and development tools and software. The company serves semiconductor companies, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), cloud service providers (CSPs), and organizations developing chips for end markets such as smartphones, consumer electronics, industrial IoT, embedded systems, cloud data centers, networking, automotive, and robotics. It provides its products and services in the United States, China, Japan, Taiwan, Korea, and internationally. The company was founded in 1990 and is based in Cambridge, United Kingdom. Arm Holdings plc operates as a subsidiary of SoftBank Group Corp.

judgment.summary: Arm Holdings exhibits strong growth and margins but carries a very high valuation and significant leverage.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter beat estimates; next earnings date is 2026-07-29.
positives: Revenue growth 20.1% YoY and earnings growth 47.9% YoY indicate strong business expansion.
Gross margin of 97.5% and profit margin of 18.4% demonstrate excellent profitability.
Quarterly earnings beat estimates by 3.6% in the last report.
Strong liquidity with a current ratio of 6.00 and quick ratio of 5.83.
negatives: Trailing P/E of 400.62 and forward P/E of 113.86 indicate an extremely high valuation.
PEG ratio of 3.50 suggests the stock may be overvalued relative to its growth.
Debt/Equity ratio of 5.93 indicates significant leverage.
Analyst mean target of $247.41 is substantially below the current spot price.

news.paragraph: Arm Holdings experienced significant volatility this week, surging on news of Nvidia's new chip announcement before seeing insider selling and a midday dip. Despite the recent price action, the company's valuation has reached historic highs, with its forward P/E ratio exceeding 113. While earnings and revenue growth remain strong, the stock's premium valuation and insider selling raise questions about sustainability.
